senses.def: small, curved piece of metal or bone or even a strong thorn, with a sharp point on one end, usually with a barb just behind the point, and a loop or bend on the other end to which a fishing line can be attached; used with some bait attached to it in order to attract a fish
senses.comment: A literal rendering of Matthew 17:27 could be quite misleading, since it would imply that only the hook was thrown into the water. What was thrown into the water was a line with a baited hook on the end, and it may be necessary to be explicit in some languages in order to avoid misunderstanding.

senses.def: a city on the coast of southern Palestine; the Ashdod of the OT

(derivative of ἄκανθα ‘thorn plant,’ 3.17) pertaining to being made or consisting of thorns; in the NT, only in the phrase ἀκάνθινον στέφανον, a crown made from a plant with sharp projections on its stem and/or branches; symbol of hardship
senses.comment: It may be necessary to indicate that this crown of thorns is one made of ‘branches of a thorny bush,’ for the crown did not consist merely of thorns but of thorny vines or branches.

senses.def: a reciprocal reference between entities
pertaining to having no defect or blemish
senses.comment: In 1 Peter 1:19 the overall context is figurative, but the immediate meaning must be regarded as literal.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being without fault and hence morally blameless
to cause to recall and to think about again
glosses: to cause to think about again

senses.def: to cause oneself to remember or to be caused to remember
relief as a cessation or suspension of trouble and difficulty
senses.comment: In rendering ‘relief to you who suffer,’ it may be necessary to restructure the semantic relations, for example, ‘to cause you who suffer not to have to suffer longer’ or ‘to cause you to no longer have to suffer.’

senses.def: a partial degree of liberty or freedom

senses.subdomain: Pass, Cross Over, Go Through, Go Around
senses.def: to pass by a point of reference on the opposite side
glosses: to pass by on the opposite side
senses.comment: There may, however, be a number of problems involved in rendering ἀντιπαρέρχομαι in Luke 10:31, for in many languages it is difficult to conceive of a road having an ‘opposite side.’ One can often render this phrase in Luke 10:31 as ‘having seen him he went on past, staying as far away from him as he could.’

senses.def: a person who has previously been a slave but is now released from slavery
a Christian of Alexandria who worked in Ephesus and Corinth
(derivative of Ἀραβία ‘Arabia,’ 93.410) a person who is a native of Arabia
one who is the head of and who directs the affairs of a synagogue
pertaining to being without offspring
pertaining to not employing one’s understanding, particularly in practical matters
senses.comment: It is possible that ἄφρων in Romans 2:20 (παιδευτὴν ἀφρόνων ‘instructor of the foolish’) refers to people who are simply uninstructed or ignorant, since ἀφρόνων could be parallel with νηπίων, occurring in the same verse. On the other hand, there appears to be a contrast in the meanings of ἀφρόνων and νηπίων because of the distinctiveness in meanings of παιδευτήν and διδάσκαλον. Therefore, ἄφρων in Romans 2:20 is better understood as referring to those who act foolishly because they do not use their potential for understanding.

senses.def: tailless amphibian with a squat body, moist smooth skin, and long hind legs for jumping; about 70 mm long; brown or olive-green; develops from tadpole; Rana esculenta (Edible frog) or Rana punctata (Spotted frog)
senses.comment: In this only reference to frogs in the NT, the connotation is of something unclean and abhorrent. In a number of societies, however, frogs are regarded as very valuable and worthwhile animals, since they are often an important source of food. On the other hand, in such areas there are usually certain types of frogs or toads which are particularly poisonous and whose names, therefore, do carry bad connotations.

senses.def: the sound of shouting or crying out
a Roman proconsul of Achaia

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: central hinge joint of the leg where the thigh is joined to the lower leg
senses.comment: In Luke 5:8 the phrase ‘fell on his knees before Jesus’ should normally not be rendered literally since it might imply accidental stumbling. A more satisfactory equivalent may be ‘knelt down before,’ as a sign of worship or gratitude.|The term γόνυ occurs in a number of idiomatic phrases in the NT. For example, in Hebrews 12:12 the command ‘to strengthen the weak knees’ should normally not be translated literally, but by an expression meaning ‘to strengthen determination’ or ‘to give courage to’ (see 25.152). The ‘bending of the knees’ in Mark 15:19 was a sign of mock respect, and in such a context the term for ‘knee’ is often semantically absorbed into an expression meaning literally ‘bow down before’ (see 53.61).

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of γόνυ[a] ‘knee,’ 8.47) a person in the attitude or position of one worshiping or submitting to authority
(a Semitic idiom, literally: the knee bends, or: the knee bows) to bend or bow the knee as a symbol of religious devotion
(an idiom, literally: straighten paralyzed knees) to gain encouragement by a strong resolve
senses.comment: See discussion at 23.170.

senses.domain: Stances and Events Related to Stances
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to place the knees, a Latinism) to kneel down before, with the implication of an act of reverence or of supplication
senses.comment: In a number of cultures, kneeling does not imply either reverence or an act of supplication. In some instances translators have used a functional substitute involving a similar type of stance, namely, ‘to bow low before,’ but it may be necessary to use a more or less literal description of ‘kneeling before’ and then to place in a marginal note an indication of the implications of such an act.

senses.def: cardinal number, where there are fourteen instances of a countable entity
senses.comment: It is possible that δεκατέσσαρες in Matthew 1:17 has a symbolic meaning in view of its being equivalent to twice seven. Others have suggested that the number fourteen is derived from the value of the name David based on the numerical values of the consonants in the Hebrew form of the name. This may explain certain of the irregularities in the listing of the generations.

senses.def: to clean out or to clean off thoroughly
to spread information extensively and effectively concerning someone or something
a division into opposing groups, generally two
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent of ‘causing division’ (Romans 16:17) is literally ‘to cause two groups in place of one group,’ but more frequently the equivalent is expressed in terms of attitudes, for example, ‘to cause people to be angry at one another’ or ‘to cause people not to like one another’ or ‘to cause people to think of one another as enemies.’

senses.def: (derivative of δωρέομαι ‘to give, to grant,’ 57.83) that which is given or granted
a person who worships idols
to be greatly astounded, with either positive or negative reactions
senses.comment: In the meaning of ‘alarmed,’ ἐκθαμβέομαι may often be rendered simply as ‘to be afraid.’

senses.def: to begin vegetative growth, with special emphasis upon the sprouting of leaves
senses.comment: The initial stages of growth, either of a plant as a whole or in the renewal of foliage after a winter or dry season, may be expressed in a number of ways, for example, ‘to become green again,’ ‘to show leaves,’ ‘to see leaves begin,’ or ‘when leaves unfold.’

senses.def: a name attributed to Jesus Christ
pertaining to being effective in causing something to happen
to send out or away from, presumably for some purpose
to send a message, presumably by someone
pertaining to being cursed
senses.comment: The occurrences of ἐπάρατος in John 7:49 and ἐπικατάρατος in Galatians 3:10 imply much more than being cursed by some person. In such contexts, the real meaning is that these individuals have already been condemned by God or are under the threat of such a condemnation.

senses.def: help, with the possible implication of assistance provided by an ally
punishing, with the implication of causing people to suffer what they deserve
pertaining to a position within an area
the result of having acquired wealth
senses.comment: It may also be convenient to translate this clause in Acts 19:25 as ‘you know that this work we do makes us rich.’ For another interpretation of εὐπορία in Acts 19:25, see εὐπορία[b] 57.201.

senses.def: an easy means of gaining a profit from one’s business or trade
glosses: easy way of making a living
senses.comment: For another interpretation of εὐπορία[a] 57.32.

senses.subdomain: Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
senses.def: to be deeply committed to something, with the implication of accompanying desire
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ζηλοῦτε in 1 Corinthians 12:31 as being indicative and therefore translated as ‘you set your hearts on the more important gifts.’

senses.def: to have a deep concern for or devotion to someone or something
glosses: to have a deep concern for
senses.comment: The Judaizers referred to in Galatians 4:17 may have been sincere, but they were misguided in their zeal.

senses.def: set one’s heart on something that belongs to someone else
senses.comment: It is, of course, also possible to render ζηλόω in James 4:2 as meaning ‘to be envious’ or ‘to be jealous’ (see 88.163).

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to experience strong envy and resentment against someone
(derivative of θησαυρός[c] ‘treasure,’ 65.10) to keep safe that which is of great value
(a figurative extension of meaning of θησαυρίζω[a] ‘to treasure up,’ 65.11) to cause something of a more extensive nature to happen in the future
glosses: to cause to happen more intensely or more extensively

senses.def: a major OT prophet
to cause to be in a place, with or without the accompanying feature of standing position
senses.comment: ἵστημι[a] may very well imply a standing position, but what is in focus is not the stance but the location.

senses.def: to acknowledge the validity of something
to establish as validated and in force
senses.comment: In rendering this expression in Hebrews 10:9 it may be necessary to indicate what is involved in ‘the first’ and ‘the second.’ The contrast is between the OT system of sacrifices and the sacrifice of Christ.

senses.def: to pay, possibly in the sense of to weigh out or to count out a sum of money

senses.subdomain: To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
senses.def: to propose or put forward a particular selection
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἵστημι in Acts 1:23, see 33.343.

senses.def: to speak of someone or something as being well qualified or suited for a particular purpose
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἵστημι in Acts 1:23, see 30.87.

senses.domain: Stances and Events Related to Stances
senses.def: to be in a standing position

senses.domain: Stances and Events Related to Stances
senses.def: to assume a standing position
senses.comment: In the context of John 7:37 Jesus has been teaching and thus would be presumably in the seated position of a rabbi, but the unusual declaration which follows this introductory statement is made somewhat more emphatic not only by Jesus standing but by his proclamation in a loud voice.

senses.def: to be in a location, with the possible implication of standing but with the focus upon location
to cease, in reference to some type of movement
to continue to exist, with the probable implication of some resistance involved
senses.comment: In a number of languages, however, it may be preferable to translate οὐ σταθήσεται in Matthew 12:25 as ‘will come to ruin’ or ‘will be destroyed.’

senses.def: to continue firmly or well-established in a particular state

senses.subdomain: Have an Opinion, Hold a View
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to stand at the heart) to continue to have an opinion
glosses: to keep on being of an opinion

senses.def: the high priest who played a prominent role in the condemnation of Jesus
(an idiom, literally: to pierce the heart) to experience acute emotional distress, implying both concern and regret
(derivative of κατηγορέω ‘to accuse,’ 33.427) the content of the accusation or charge made against someone
senses.comment: It is possible that in 1 Timothy 5:19 κατηγορία may denote either the event of accusing or the content of the accusation. If κατηγορία in 1 Timothy 5:19 is understood as the event of accusing, it may be classified with the items in 33.427.

senses.def: (derivative of κηρύσσω[c] ‘to preach,’ 33.256) a person who preaches
a piece of furniture used for sleeping
senses.comment: It is not necessary to understand Luke 11:7 to mean that the children were in the same bed with the man, but it is, of course, possible that the reference here is to a relatively humble house in which all the members of the family would sleep on a single raised platform. See also 10.37.

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of κοίτη[a] ‘bed,’ 6.108) to have sexual relations
senses.comment: In some languages one may speak of ‘sexual life’ as ‘the way one lives with one’s wife’ or ‘how one treats one’s wife.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to engage in immoral sexual excess
(an idiom, literally: to have bed, though in combination with ἔχω, κοίτη early acquired the metonymic meaning of sexual relations) to be in a state of pregnancy
senses.comment: This expression contrasts with the meaning of συλλαμβάνω[b], 23.49, in that it seems to focus more upon the state of pregnancy rather than the event of conception.

senses.def: pertaining to being superior to something else in characteristics or function

senses.subdomain: High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
senses.def: pertaining to having a higher status in comparison to something else
small flying insect; feeds on human or animal blood; regarded as pest
senses.comment: The straining of liquids referred to in Matthew 23:24 is based on the regulations in Leviticus 11, in which the gnat is the smallest of the unclean creatures and the camel the largest.|For the only occurrence of κώνωψ in the NT, one may use a term which refers to any small flying insect which might fall into a beverage and thus have to be strained out.

senses.def: (a Latin name) a group of people, presumably Jews, who had been slaves but later obtained their freedom; their synagogue was also known by the same name
pertaining to being without any result
to change one’s thinking about something
senses.comment: In Acts 28:6 μεταβάλλομαι may often be expressed as ‘to no longer think as they did’ or ‘to think differently now.’

senses.def: to behave in the same manner as someone else
to find fault with someone by implying blame
the founder of a sect (not occurring in the NT, but see 93.282)
one of the seven helpers in the church in Jerusalem
to be on a journey, presumably with the focus upon being en route
to associate with one another, normally involving spacial proximity and/or joint activity, and usually implying some kind of reciprocal relation or involvement
glosses: to be in the company of
senses.comment: In translating terms referring to association, one may employ a number of different kinds of expressions, for example, ‘to have something to do with,’ ‘to keep company with,’ ‘to go around with,’ ‘to join in doing things together,’ or ‘to become a companion of.’ Sometimes association is spoken of in terms of the impression made upon others, for example, ‘to be seen often together,’ ‘to be regarded as close friends,’ and even idiomatically as ‘to be another person’s shadow.’

senses.def: the early part of the daylight period

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Units of Time: Daybreak, Midday, Midnight, Late
senses.def: the point of time when the day begins
to serve with a view to impressing others
glosses: to serve in order to call attention to oneself

senses.def: to come to be present at a particular place
to come to the assistance of someone
to come to be in a place
to cause something to happen by introducing factors from outside
to experience something which is adverse and severe

senses.subdomain: Hold a Wrong View, Be Mistaken
senses.def: (figurative extension of meaning of πλανάω ‘to cause to wander off the path,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause someone to hold a wrong view and thus be mistaken
senses.comment: To mislead people as to proper views which they should have may often be expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to twist people’s thoughts,’ ‘to cause what is false to seem like what is true,’ ‘to make a lie appear true,’ ‘to dig away the truth,’ or ‘to cover the eyes with lies.’

senses.def: to move about, without definite destination or particular purpose
to no longer believe what is true, but to start believing what is false
senses.comment: Though in some languages one can preserve the figurative meaning of ‘to wander’ or ‘to go astray’ in connection with truth, it is not possible to do so in many languages, and therefore it may be necessary to spell out in some detail precisely what is involved, for example, ‘to stop believing what is true and to start believing what is false.’

senses.def: a public official responsible for administrative matters within a town or city and a member of the ruling council of such a political unit

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being gentle and mild
to be worried or anxious beforehand or in advance

senses.domain: Stances and Events Related to Stances
senses.subdomain: Prostrate as an Act of Reverence or Supplication
senses.def: to prostrate oneself before someone, implying supplication
senses.comment: A strictly literal translation of προσπίπτω[a] or πίπτω[c], namely, ‘to fall down before,’ can be entirely misleading in that it may suggest an accident caused by stumbling or tripping. It may therefore be necessary in a number of languages to translate ‘to bow down low before’ or ‘to bow down to the ground before.’

senses.def: to strike against some object

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: a dead body, whether of an animal or a human being
senses.comment: In the parallel to Matthew 24:28 (Luke 17:37), the term σῶμα (8.1) occurs. Since in some languages one must distinguish varying degrees of decomposition of a corpse, it may be important in certain contexts to indicate whether the body is of a person or an animal which has recently died or one which has undergone considerable decomposition.

senses.def: a rapid motion, especially of the eye
senses.comment: For ῥιπή as part of an idiom, see 67.114.

senses.def: a city on the coast of Phoenicia between Tyre and Sidon
any kind of edible grain, though generally referring to wheat
the plant of wheat
senses.comment: Elsewhere in the NT σῖτος, when used alone, refers to wheat as grain, but even in John 12:24 τοῦ σίτου may be interpreted as a so-called ‘appositional genitive,’ that is, ‘seed which is wheat’ or ‘wheat seed.’|While in some parts of the world wheat as a grain or as a plant is not known, in almost all instances people are acquainted with wheat flour, and therefore it is often possible to translate ‘wheat’ as ‘flour plant’ or ‘plant the grain of which is used to make flour.’ In some languages, however, the only possible equivalent is ‘rice-like plant’ in which ‘rice-like’ means essentially ‘grass-like,’ while at the same time indicating edible grain.

senses.def: a Roman military unit of about six hundred soldiers, though only a part of such a cohort was often referred to as a cohort

senses.subdomain: Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
senses.def: a long, flowing robe
senses.comment: The cultural significance of ‘long robe’ would be high social status and dignified occupation or activity.

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of συλαγωγέω ‘to carry off as booty or as captive in war,’ not occurring in the NT) to take over complete control of a person as one would a captive
senses.comment: In some languages it is possible to preserve the figurative meaning of συλαγωγέω in Colossians 2:8 by employing a simile, for example, ‘see that no one makes you a kind of captive by human wisdom’ or ‘see to it that no one uses human wisdom and by this means makes you, so to speak, a captive.’

senses.def: to associate with one another, normally involving spacial proximity and/or joint activity, and usually implying some kind of reciprocal relation or involvement
glosses: to be in the company of
senses.comment: In translating terms referring to association, one may employ a number of different kinds of expressions, for example, ‘to have something to do with,’ ‘to keep company with,’ ‘to go around with,’ ‘to join in doing things together,’ or ‘to become a companion of.’ Sometimes association is spoken of in terms of the impression made upon others, for example, ‘to be seen often together,’ ‘to be regarded as close friends,’ and even idiomatically as ‘to be another person’s shadow.’

senses.subdomain: Kinship Relations of the Same Generation
senses.def: a person offered parental care and/or adoption along with the reference person, though not related by blood
senses.comment: It is possible, however, that σύντροφος in Acts 13:1 has the meaning of ‘a close friend from childhood’ (see 34.15).|In some languages ‘a foster brother’ may be referred to as ‘a person who becomes a brother by being adopted’ or ‘a person who grows up just as though he were a brother.’

senses.def: a close friend on the basis of having been brought up together
senses.comment: Some scholars, however, understand σύντροφος in Acts 13:1 as being an instance of σύντροφος[a] 'foster brother' (see 10.51).

senses.def: to be sorrowful and complain, presumably on the basis of wretched circumstances
cardinal number, where there are four hundred instances of a countable entity
a well-worn path or thoroughfare
a person who defected from true faith
a relatively small part which continues to exist

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being evil in the sense of moral baseness
an area along the seacoast to the west and north of Palestine

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Agriculture and Husbandry
senses.def: items used to control the actions of a horse, consisting of a bit (a short metal bar placed in the mouth of a horse) and bridle (ropes or leather straps attached to the bit and fitted over the horse’s head)
senses.comment: In languages in which a bit or bridle as a piece of harness is not known, one can employ a descriptive phrase, ‘something to guide a horse with’ or ‘something to put in the mouth of a horse to guide it.’|In Revelation 14:20 the reference to a bit and bridle is merely an indication of measurement, that is to say, the height of the bit and bridle from the ground, and one may reinterpret this measurement as ‘about a meter and a half’ or ‘about five feet.’

senses.def: economic resources, usually implying an abundance of such assets
a generic term for currency, occurring mostly in the plural
glosses: money (normally a reference to actual coins)
senses.comment: It would also be possible to translate ἤνεγκεν τὸ χρῆμα in Acts 4:37 as ‘he brought the proceeds from the sale.’|In Acts 8:18 (προσήνεγκεν αὐτοῖς χρήματα ‘he offered them money’) the reference of χρήματα would appear to be cash.

senses.def: the last in an inclusive series beginning with ἄλφα (61.7), implying an all-inclusive sphere of authority and high status
senses.comment: For a discussion of the relationship of ω to ἄλφα and its different translations, see 61.7.
